description: A stored procedure's unqualified and partially-qualified object references resolve against the procedure's HOME database and schema - where the procedure LIVES - matching Snowflake, and not against the caller's current database. LIB.UTIL.SAVE_ENTRY internally calls UTIL.IS_ALLOWED and merges into UTIL.SETTINGS, so both must resolve against LIB.UTIL when the procedure is invoked while APPDB.WORK is current; the MERGE landing in lib.util.settings is what proves it. The caller's context is RESTORED after the call, so CURRENT_DATABASE and CURRENT_SCHEMA still read APPDB and WORK. And the internal function call really runs, so an invalid code is still detected across databases and nothing is written. Converted 1:1 from scripting/ProcedureHomeSchemaResolutionTest (now retired).

steps.sql: CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS lib
USE DATABASE lib
CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS util
USE SCHEMA util
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION UTIL.IS_ALLOWED(code VARCHAR) RETURNS BOOLEAN LANGUAGE SQL AS $$ UPPER(code) IN ('A', 'B', 'C') $$
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE UTIL.SETTINGS (name VARCHAR, label VARCHAR, code VARCHAR)

CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE UTIL.SAVE_ENTRY(p_name VARCHAR, p_label VARCHAR, p_code VARCHAR) RETURNS VARCHAR LANGUAGE SQL AS $$ BEGIN IF (NOT UTIL.IS_ALLOWED(:p_code)) THEN RETURN 'invalid'; END IF; MERGE INTO UTIL.SETTINGS t USING (SELECT :p_name AS name, :p_label AS label) s ON t.name = s.name AND t.label = s.label WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT (name, label, code) VALUES (:p_name, :p_label, :p_code); RETURN 'saved'; END $$
CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS appdb
USE DATABASE appdb
CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS work
USE SCHEMA work
CALL lib.util.save_entry('n1', 'label1', 'A')
SELECT name, label, code FROM lib.util.settings
